items.title: Section: Fascicle 45 Opens — the Factors of Awakening Continue With the Sixth of Fifteen Topics, the Four Correct Reliances

items.zh: 云何菩薩修正四依？謂諸菩薩為求義故，從他聽法，不為求世藻飾文詞。菩薩求義不為求文而聽法時，雖遇常流言音說法，但依於義，恭敬聽受。
items.en: From the Bodhisattva Stage within the Basic Section, the chapter on the initial yoga foundation, chapter seventeen, part two: the factors of awakening. How do bodhisattvas correctly cultivate the four reliances? Bodhisattvas who, seeking the meaning of the teaching, listen to the dharma from another, not seeking worldly, ornamental phrasing — when bodhisattvas seeking meaning rather than phrasing listen to the teaching, even when they encounter it delivered in the most ordinary, common speech, they nonetheless rely on its meaning, listening to and receiving it with reverence.

items.title: Section: Relying on the Teaching, Not on Whoever Happens to Deliver It — Recognising Provisional and Complete Teaching for What Each Actually Is

items.zh: 又諸菩薩如實了知闇說、大說；如實知已，以理為依，不由耆長、眾所知識補特伽羅、若佛、若僧所說法故即便信受，是故不依補特伽羅。如是菩薩以理為依，補特伽羅非所依故，於真實義心不動搖，於正法中他緣匪奪。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly recognise provisional teaching and complete teaching for what each is; having recognised this correctly, they rely on principle, not believing and accepting something as true merely because an elder, a well-known figure, or the Buddha or the community are said to have taught it — and for this reason they do not rely on the person. In this way, bodhisattvas rely on principle rather than on the person, and their mind remains unshaken regarding genuine truth, never pulled away by some other influence within the true teaching.

items.title: Section: Relying on Scriptures of Complete and Final Meaning, Never on Those Still Provisional — Why a Provisional Teaching Can Always, in Principle, Be Overturned

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於如來所深殖正信、深殖清淨，一向澄清；唯依如來了義經典，非不了義。了義經典為所依故，於佛所說法毘奈耶不可引奪。何以故？以佛所說不了義經，依種種門辯本性義，猶未決定，尚生疑惑，非了義故。若諸菩薩於了義經不決定者，於佛所說法毘奈耶猶可引奪。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas who have deeply planted correct faith and deeply planted purity towards the Tathāgata, entirely and thoroughly clarified, rely exclusively on the Tathāgata's scriptures of complete and final meaning, never on those of provisional meaning. Because they rely on scriptures of complete and final meaning, nothing can pull them away from what the Buddha has taught in the dharma and the discipline. Why is this so? Because the provisional scriptures the Buddha spoke explain the underlying nature of things through varying approaches, not yet settled, still capable of provoking doubt, since they are not of complete and final meaning. Should bodhisattvas remain unsettled regarding scriptures of complete and final meaning, they remain vulnerable to being pulled away, even within what the Buddha has taught in the dharma and the discipline.

items.title: Section: Relying on Realised Wisdom, Never on Mere Learning — Closing the Four Reliances, the Four Standards They Establish, and Their Power to Guide Beings Fully Out of Affliction

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於真證智見為真實，非於聞思但識法義非真證智。是諸菩薩如實了知修所成智所應知者，非唯聞思所成諸識所能了達。如實知已，聞如來說最極甚深所有法義，終不誹毀。是名菩薩修正四依。依正四依善修習故，略顯四量。謂所說義、正理、大師修所成慧真實證智。又諸菩薩一切四依為所依止，精勤發起正加行故，於出要道明了開示，無有迷惑。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas regard wisdom genuinely realised through direct insight as true, not the mere understanding of the teaching's meaning gained only through learning and reflection, which is not genuinely realised wisdom. Such bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly recognise that what should be known through wisdom accomplished by cultivation is not something the consciousnesses accomplished only by learning and reflection are capable of fully comprehending. Having correctly recognised this, upon hearing the Tathāgata teach the most extremely profound dharma of every kind, they never disparage it. This is called a bodhisattva's correct cultivation of the four reliances. Because bodhisattvas skilfully cultivate the four correct reliances, four standards of measure are thereby, in brief, revealed: the meaning that is spoken, correct principle, the genuine teacher, and the true, realised wisdom accomplished by cultivation. Furthermore, bodhisattvas who take all four reliances as their basis, diligently arousing correct practice, are able to clearly explain the essential path leading out of affliction, entirely without confusion.

items.title: Section: The Four Unhindered Understandings — Teaching, Meaning, Language, and Eloquence, Each Resting on Both the Comprehensive Detail and the Essential Nature of Every Phenomenon

items.zh: 云何菩薩所修菩薩四無礙解？謂諸菩薩，於一切法一切異門，盡所有性、如所有性，依修所成無所滯礙無退轉智，是名菩薩法無礙解。又諸菩薩，於一切法一切異相，盡所有性、如所有性，依修所成無所滯礙無退轉智，是名菩薩義無礙解。又諸菩薩，於一切法一切釋詞，盡所有性、如所有性，依修所成無所滯礙無退轉智，是名菩薩詞無礙解。又諸菩薩，於一切法一切品別，盡所有性、如所有性，依修所成無所滯礙無退轉智，是名菩薩辯無礙解。
items.en: What are the four unhindered understandings bodhisattvas cultivate? Bodhisattvas who, regarding every teaching-approach to every phenomenon, comprehend both its exhaustive particulars and its essential nature, relying on an unhindered, unregressing wisdom accomplished through cultivation — this is called a bodhisattva's unhindered understanding of the teaching. Bodhisattvas who, regarding every distinct aspect of every phenomenon, comprehend both its exhaustive particulars and its essential nature through this same wisdom — this is called a bodhisattva's unhindered understanding of meaning. Bodhisattvas who, regarding every mode of explanation for every phenomenon, comprehend both its exhaustive particulars and its essential nature through this same wisdom — this is called a bodhisattva's unhindered understanding of language. Bodhisattvas who, regarding every category and distinction among phenomena, comprehend both its exhaustive particulars and its essential nature through this same wisdom — this is called a bodhisattva's unhindered eloquence.

items.title: Section: The Four Unhindered Understandings' Benefit — Five Kinds of Skilful Mastery, and the Awakening That Nothing Beyond Them Can Produce

items.zh: 若諸菩薩依是菩薩四無礙解，應知獲得無量最勝五處善巧。一、蘊善巧，二、界善巧，三、處善巧，四、緣起善巧，五、處非處善巧。菩薩由此四種行相，於一切法自能妙善現正等覺，亦善為他無倒開示。此上無有自能妙善現正等覺，況善為他無倒開示。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who rely on these four unhindered understandings should be understood to obtain immeasurable, supreme skilful mastery in five domains: first, mastery of the aggregates; second, mastery of the elements; third, mastery of the sense-bases; fourth, mastery of dependent origination; fifth, mastery of the possible and the impossible. Through these four modes of understanding, bodhisattvas are themselves able, regarding every phenomenon, to wondrously and skilfully manifest complete, correct awakening, and are also able to skilfully explain it to others without any distortion. Beyond this, there is nothing capable of enabling a bodhisattva to wondrously and skilfully manifest complete, correct awakening themselves — let alone skilfully explain it to others without distortion.

items.title: Section: The Provisions for Awakening Open — Merit and Wisdom, Ripening in Three Tiers Across Three Incalculable Eons

items.zh: 云何菩薩菩提資糧？當知如是菩提資糧，略有二種。一者、福德資糧，二者、智慧資糧。此二資糧廣分別義，如前所說自他利品，應知其相。又此福德、智慧資糧，菩薩於初無數大劫所修習者，應知名下；若於第二無數大劫所修習者，應知名中；若於第三無數大劫所修習者、應知名上。
items.en: What are a bodhisattva's provisions for awakening? One should understand that these provisions for awakening are, in brief, of two kinds: first, the provision of merit; second, the provision of wisdom. The full, detailed meaning of these two provisions is as already explained in the earlier chapter on benefiting self and others, and their characteristics should be understood accordingly. Furthermore, regarding this provision of merit and provision of wisdom, whatever bodhisattvas cultivate during the first incalculable great eon should be understood as the lesser tier; whatever is cultivated during the second incalculable great eon should be understood as the middling tier; and whatever is cultivated during the third incalculable great eon should be understood as the supreme tier.

items.title: Section: The Thirty-Seven Classical Factors Reconceived — A Bodhisattva Understands Them Fully Without Ever Rushing to Realise Them

items.zh: 云何菩薩於三十七菩提分法精勤修習？謂諸菩薩，依止菩薩四無礙解，由善方便所攝妙智，於三十七菩提分法如實了知，而不作證。是諸菩薩，普於一切二乘理趣三十七種菩提分法皆如實知。謂於聲聞乘理趣及於大乘理趣三十七種菩提分法皆如實知。於聲聞乘理趣三十七種菩提分法如實了知，如聲聞地，如前所說一切應知。
items.en: How do bodhisattvas diligently cultivate the thirty-seven factors of awakening? Bodhisattvas who, relying on the four unhindered understandings, through the wondrous wisdom encompassed by skilful means, correctly and thoroughly understand the thirty-seven factors of awakening, yet do not realise them. Such bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly know the thirty-seven factors of awakening across both approaches belonging to the two vehicles — that is, they correctly and thoroughly know the thirty-seven factors of awakening according to both the śrāvaka vehicle's own approach and the great vehicle's own approach. Their correct and thorough knowledge of the thirty-seven factors of awakening according to the śrāvaka vehicle's approach is exactly as already explained in the Śrāvaka Stage, and should be understood accordingly.

blocks.text: Fascicle 45 opens. The chapter on the factors of awakening continues with its sixth to fourteenth topics. Today: the four reliances, the four unhindered understandings, the provisions for awakening, and a new way of holding the thirty-seven factors.

"Bodhisattvas listen to the dharma seeking its meaning, not worldly ornamental phrasing." Master Cháng Bǎi: even when the speaker uses plain, everyday language, the bodhisattva grasps the meaning the words convey.

They rely on principle, not accepting something merely because an elder, a well-known person, the Buddha, or the community said it. Master Cháng Bǎi: the principle was laid down against flattering, deceitful beings; what one has genuinely realised cannot easily be shaken.

Provisional scriptures "explain the nature of things through varying approaches, not yet settled, still provoking doubt". Master Cháng Bǎi: the obscure teaching is provisional, the great teaching definitive. Venerable Miào Jìng: faith that rests on wisdom deeply realising the ultimate is "deeply planted correct faith".

The reliances reveal four standards: the meaning spoken, correct principle, the teacher, and the true wisdom realised through practice. Both lecturers: "the teacher" here corresponds to relying on definitive scriptures. Master Cháng Bǎi: this counters those who treat merely hearing the dharma as the end and will not go on to reflect and practise.

Of teaching, meaning, language, and eloquence. Master Cháng Bǎi: the "exhaustive particulars" concern phenomena, the "essential nature" concerns principle. Venerable Miào Jìng: all four are achieved on the ninth ground, Good Wisdom.

Mastery of the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, dependent origination, and the possible and impossible. Venerable Miào Jìng admitted frankly that for a long time he did not know how to explain this passage: "but I'm slow; clever people may find it easier."

Merit and wisdom are cultivated across three incalculable eons: lesser in the first, middling in the second, supreme in the third. Master Cháng Bǎi: in the first eon the two emptinesses are not yet realised, so the provisions are still mixed with grasping. The four immeasurables belong to merit; dependent origination and the like to wisdom.

"Through wondrous wisdom encompassed by skilful means, they thoroughly understand the thirty-seven factors, yet do not realise them." Master Cháng Bǎi: to benefit beings, they keep some seeds of affliction so as to go on taking birth in the world.

The four reliances are among the most quoted lines in Mahāyāna Buddhism, and they apply to how you read this treatise, too: listen for the meaning, test it by principle, and let your own practice be the final judge.

quiz.q: When bodhisattvas listen to the dharma from another, what do they seek?
options: the meaning, not worldly ornamental phrasing
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas listen to the dharma seeking its meaning, not worldly ornamental phrasing." Venerable Miào Jìng: stated in full, this is "rely on meaning, not on words"; beautiful phrasing without the ultimate meaning cannot satisfy.

quiz.q: Relying on principle, bodhisattvas do not accept a teaching merely because of whom?
options: not because an elder, a well-known person, or the Buddha or the community are said to have taught it
quiz.why: "They rely on principle, not accepting something merely because an elder, a well-known person, the Buddha, or the community are said to have taught it." Venerable Miào Jìng: not because someone is old or famous. Master Cháng Bǎi: not just because someone looks dignified.

quiz.q: Cultivating the four reliances reveals which four standards of measure?
options: the meaning spoken, correct principle, the teacher, wisdom realised through cultivation
quiz.why: "Four standards are revealed: the meaning that is spoken, correct principle, the teacher, and the true wisdom realised through cultivation." Master Cháng Bǎi: the third, the teacher, corresponds to relying on definitive scriptures.

quiz.q: Which unhindered understanding concerns every mode of explanation (釋辭)?
quiz.why: Unhindered wisdom regarding every mode of explanation of every phenomenon is the unhindered understanding of language. Master Cháng Bǎi: mastering the dialects of many places freely.

quiz.q: Relying on the four, which five masteries does a bodhisattva obtain?
options: aggregates, elements, sense-bases, dependent origination, the possible and impossible
quiz.why: Mastery of the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, dependent origination, and the possible and impossible. Master Cháng Bǎi: what does not contradict the facts is "possible," what contradicts them "impossible."

quiz.q: How does the treatise grade the provisions across three incalculable eons?
options: first eon lesser, second middling, third supreme
quiz.why: What is cultivated in the first incalculable eon is lesser, in the second middling, in the third supreme. Venerable Miào Jìng: to travel far you must carry provisions.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas fully understand the thirty-seven factors, yet what?
quiz.why: "Through wondrous wisdom encompassed by skilful means, they thoroughly understand the thirty-seven factors, yet do not realise them." Venerable Miào Jìng: realising them would end birth and death and enter the unconditioned — one would rest.
